assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moiré quantum matter as a tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. Originality is high and the impact spans a very large community. It is close to the kind of surprise that two-dimensional materials keep delivering, and the continuum-model band structure is a clean electronic-structure result.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. The credited trio maps naturally onto a theory-plus-experiment prize. Other contributors (for example in related earlier twisted-bilayer theory or in parallel experiments) are not in the supplied credit, so I rely only on these three.
assessment.maturity: Experiments have been reproduced by many groups and the field is very active, so confirmation is strong. The interpretation of the superconducting and correlated phases is still debated, but the discovery itself is stable. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain unsettled.
Whether other earlier theorists deserve credit is not resolvable from the supplied names; this is from my own recollection and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method unified density functional theory with molecular dynamics, enabling parameter-free simulation of bonding changes, liquids, defects and chemical reactions at finite temperature. Originality and clarity are exceptional and it is among the most widely used computational methods in condensed matter and chemistry. I rate it highly from my own work in first-principles methods, while recognising a risk of bias toward my own subfield.
assessment.attribution: Credit is unusually clean: the 1985 paper is by Car and Parrinello, and the two-person configuration is the natural one. Many later extensions (Born-Oppenheimer MD, linear scaling, etc.) are not credited here and do not need to be.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use make the impact fully established. Timing is overdue rather than premature. The remaining question is whether a computational method is judged a physics prize rather than a chemistry one, given the 1998 chemistry prize for density functional theory.
uncertainties: Prize-category fit between physics and chemistry given prior DFT recognition.
A method prize competes with discovery-oriented candidates in committee preference.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells launched the topological-insulator field, with consequences for band-structure classification, spin-orbit-driven surface states and spintronics. The discovery is conceptually clear and has lasting influence on materials theory.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational graphene-based prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation. This supplied trio is a fair prize configuration, but the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional work by others fall outside the supplied names, so some allocation remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations, including three-dimensional topological insulators and ARPES studies, make this mature. Recognition is timely, though the topological theme has received prior prizes (2016), which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction and for three-dimensional topological insulators is outside the supplied names and may be disputed.
Overlap with the 2016 topological prize in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides, then rapid increase of Tc above 50 K, opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors beyond cuprates and stimulated work on multiband magnetism-superconductivity interplay. Importance is high and electronic-structure theory (Fermi-surface nesting, spin fluctuations) played a central role.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group reported the initial LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx superconductivity; Chen and Zhao's groups quickly raised Tc with rare-earth substitution. I selected Hosono and Zhao as the most defensible pair, but the choice between Chen and Zhao is somewhat arbitrary on the supplied record and depends on facts I have not verified.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed broadly, the materials family is well established. The pairing mechanism is still debated and no room-temperature route has emerged, which tempers lasting impact relative to cuprates.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hosono, Chen and Zhao is uncertain; precise priority for high-Tc values is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory gave exact solutions for two-dimensional critical phenomena, with deep influence on statistical mechanics, string theory and the classification of universality classes. Originality and lasting influence are very high. As a magnetism theorist I value the connection to critical phenomena, though the work is far from my own methods.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 BPZ paper is the decisive contribution and the three credited names form a natural trio. Other important contributors to the conformal bootstrap and to Virasoro-based solutions are outside the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Mature for four decades, with extensive verification in condensed-matter systems. The weakness is not maturity but the fact that the theory is formal and the prize committee has rarely rewarded purely theoretical constructions without direct experiment.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel committee would regard this as physics discovery or mathematical physics.
Credit relative to Kadanoff, Fisher and Wilson, who are not in the list, is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and underpin tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. This is a clear invention with measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Jun Ye's group pushed accuracy and many-body clock physics. Both are well matched to a two-person award. Other clock developers are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many laboratories now operate lattice clocks and confirmation is excellent. Redefinition of the second is pending, so recognition may follow that milestone; some may argue it is slightly early.
uncertainties: Competition with ion-clock work, which is not in the supplied credit.
Timing relative to the pending SI redefinition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The spin Hall effect, predicted by Dyakonov and Perel and observed in semiconductors, connects spin-orbit coupling to charge-spin conversion and is central to modern spintronics and spin-orbit torque devices. I know this area well from magnetisation dynamics and find it consequential.
assessment.attribution: Dyakonov made the original prediction; Awschalom and Jungwirth made the decisive experimental observations in semiconductors. Credit for the metallic and inverse spin Hall effects, and for theoretical intrinsic spin Hall work, lies partly outside the supplied names and may be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many systems and widely used. Recognition is timely, though the proliferation of related effects makes a sharp attribution harder.
uncertainties: Intrinsic versus extrinsic origin and priority among related contributors, not credited here.
Dyakonov's age and the committee's view of historical priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration of intrinsic ferromagnetism in atomically thin CrI3 and Cr2Ge2Te6 overturned expectations from the Mermin-Wagner theorem under anisotropy and gave a platform for two-dimensional magnetism and magnetic heterostructures. This sits close to my own interests in magnetism and for me is a conceptually clear surprise.
assessment.attribution: The 2017 experiments came from Xiang Zhang's and Xiaodong Xu's groups; the pairing of the two groups is plausible. Jarillo-Herrero's credit relates to other work and I leave him out; other co-authors on those papers are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and the field has grown quickly, but it is still young, and applications are not yet realised. Recognition may be premature relative to the other candidates.
uncertainties: Ten years of history is short; long-term impact is not yet clear.
Allocation between two simultaneous discovery groups and their student first authors.
